prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1180; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claimant reports a knee injury. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver of the vehicle involved is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. Opened bodily injury and property damage feature files.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as the claimant described it. The other driver's account matches the claimant's in every detail that was discussed.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. It lists the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle at the time of impact, consistent with statements from both the claimant and witnesses.

Entry 5: Reviewed scene photographs and a statement from an independent witness. Both support the account of how the collision occurred. Vehicle damage appears largely consistent with the described impact.

Entry 6: Obtained the vehicle's prior repair history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Claimant's attorney submitted the initial medical records. The reported knee injury is a plausible result of a collision of this type.

Entry 8: Reviewed the claimant's medical history with the attorney's office. No prior injury to the same body area is known, and the claimant has told the same account of the accident in every conversation so far.

Entry 9: Treatment began with a standard course of physical therapy and imaging. Records show the care followed a typical progression for this type of injury.

Entry 10: Medical updates indicate steady improvement. Therapy visits have been reducing in frequency as the claimant's condition gets better.

Entry 11: Received follow-up records showing treatment has tapered off as expected. The claimant has not reported any new symptoms or additional providers.

Entry 12: Reviewed the full file with the supervisor. The claim appears consistent throughout, and the injury and damage align with the reported accident. Next step is to finalize the medical evaluation with the attorney's office.
